en: I was told, "I will send it again if you lose it." Please stop by anytime.
You're not going to pick anything up? Hope to see you again.
I currently don't have anything to give you. Please come again.

Oh, Uncle Kaz! I really wish I had
some <Color:8>Toughness Z<Color:Default>!
(Haruka wants me to get her some <Color:8>Toughness Z<Color:Default>...)
Coming to a place like this always helps me to relax.
Relax? Why's that?
Because it's all nice and cozy. It kind of reminds me of my own room.
You can't possibly have as much stuff in your room as this. I'd imagined you'd be a neat freak, actually.
Yeah, I don't really have a lot of things. My room's so small, I hardly have the space anyway!
Why do you live there if it's so small?
It's my parents' place. There weren't enough rooms for me, my brother, and my sister, so I have to share my room with her.
That sounds like fun. I've had to share rooms with other people before, too.
Wow, and you had fun? Not me. My sister and I are always bickering.
Yeah, but that's normal. If you lived alone, you wouldn't have anyone to argue with even if you wanted to.
If you leave home, you might enjoy your freedom at first, but I'll bet you'd get lonely pretty fast.
Yeah, I guess you've got me there. ♪ I definitely crave attention, so if nobody's around I always go looking for someone to hang out with.
When I do eventually leave home, I'll probably get myself a roommate to help fill that void. Guess I'm not meant for living on my own.
I see. Still, I think it's worth living on your own at least once in your life.
That sounds cramped. Your brother gets a room to himself?
My brother lives in the attic.
The attic? Wow, that sounds pretty old-school. What kind of house do you live in?
Uh, just a normal one I guess. It's only about thirty years old.
Heh. That's still older than you are.
Yeah. Apparently, my dad owned it before getting married to my mom.
I guess they just never expected their family would get so big!
Hey, as long as you're all happy.
Why don't you move out? I'm sure you must have enough money to make rent.
Yeah, but I really have no need to live in a larger place. I'd rather stick it out at home  and not waste the money.
You don't want to leave home at all? Wanting to strike out on your own is pretty common among people your age.
Hmm, I guess I just don't feel it. I'd rather help my parents pay their living expenses.
Wow, you financially support your parents? That's great.
I know, right? So I don't mind living in that small room, unless something changes in my current situation.
That makes sense.
That <Color:8>Protective Amulet<Color:Default> might bring me good luck!  With your support, I could become the number one girl at the club! <Color:255,200,200,255>⑮<Color:Default>
(Hinata really seems to have her eye on that <Color:8>Protective Amulet<Color:Default>.)
Uncle Kaz! I want a <Color:8>Braised Pork Burger Set<Color:Default>! Please? It'll put a smile on my face!
(Hmm. Looks like Haruka wants a <Color:8>Braised Pork Burger Set<Color:Default>.)
Aw, but I wanted a <Color:8>Braised Pork Burger Set<Color:Default>. Now I'm frowning...
Thank you, Uncle Kaz! That was really yummy!
Welcome. Will you be taking out or dining in?
Take out.
Take out, please.
I'll take it with me.
Thank you. Here's the menu.
I'll eat here.
I'd like to eat here, please.
Eatin' here.
I'm eating here.
I'll eat here, please.
Hello, sir. What can I do for you today?
Certainly. What would you like to buy?
Of course. What would you like to sell?
How was it? Have a good game? Thanks for stopping by.
Want to play shogi? It's 500 yen a game.
Sure. I'll play.
Yes, please. I want to play.
Great! Who would you like to challenge?
Good luck to you, then.
Ah, a board with a move limit. When you play on this board, you have to corner your opponent within a set number of moves.
You can take back any move as often as you like,   so you can rely on a bit of trial and error to solve the puzzle. Enjoy the challenge.
Sorry, no. Not right now.
I'm sorry, I'm not going to play.
Okay, then. Drop in whenever you want to play.
Tell me about this place.
What's this place about?
So what is this place, anyway?
Can you tell me more about your shop?
I haven't seen you much in this place, buddy. So you wanna start playing shogi? That's great to hear.
At our place, you can play ranked matches if you're aiming for the top, and shogi Challenges to test your skill.
In a ranked match, you pick opponents closest to your current ranking. If you wanna play against tough players, you'll have to climb the ranks.
As far as ranks are concerned, by beating opponents higher rank than you, you'll take their rank. Just aim to keep going up and up.
The board is a bit special when it comes to Challenges. When you start off, the board'll be more advantageous for you, but it'll gradually get harder.
It'll cost you 500 yen to play, but you can get some nice prizes if you win. Good luck.
What's that buddy, you got no money? Come back when you have 500 yen.
Welcome! We're celebrating the emergence of a new Shogi King. For the duration, you can play with us for free.
Yeah, sure. Let me play.
Got it. Who would you like to challenge?
Sure. You're exchanging your Shogi Points? What would you like back?
Sure thing. Come again.
Way to go, champ! You're now the top mahjong  player in Kamurocho!
Now it's your turn to defend your title.
Defend my title?
Mahjong players will work their way up the ranks in order to challenge the best player. As of right now, that's you!
How long you hold on to the title⑬that's all on you. You control your own destiny.
Okay, champ. Be ready to fight to retain your crown as Kamurocho's best!
Good going out there.
It looks like you're keeping your challengers at bay. Keep the wins coming, champ.
How was it? I trust you had a good time? I hope you come visit us again soon.
Come on back whenever you want to try climbing the ranks.
'Ey boss. Would you like to exchange your winnings for prizes or purchase mahjong sticks? Or would you like to participate in the Seiryo Cup?
You need mahjong sticks to play mahjong. How much you lookin' to buy? It's 1 yen a stick.
I'll take 100,000 points worth.
Thank you. Enjoy yourself.
I'll take 25,000 points worth.
I'll take 10,000 points worth.
I'm fine for now.
I see. Come visit again sometime.
'Ey boss, you don't have enough to pay for that! Come back again when you do!
You'd like to exchange points, eh? What'll it be?
Thanks for comin' by. You're always welcome here.
Here, we hold the Mahjong Ranking Seiryo Cup, where players compete to determine the best mahjong player in Kamurocho.
You're back again! Want to participate in the Seiryo Cup?
Everyone who's anyone in the mahjong scene is taking part.
It's 50,000 yen to sign up for the rankings. Once you're signed up, you can play mahjong whenever you want.
You'll be able to earn better and better prizes each time your rank goes up.
If you manage to reach the top of the rankings, you'll win somethin' that'll really make your eyes pop.
How about it? Want to see if you can make it to the top?
Hmm... Sure, sign me up.
Okay! The registration fee is 50,000 yen. You've gotta pay in advance, sorry.
Thank you. Want to play right away?
Yeah, I'll give it a shot.
Well then, good luck, buddy.
Not now. Maybe later, though.
I see. Well, you're signed up now, so you can play ranked matches whenever you want.
(I don't have enough cash.)
Seems you're short on funds there.
Well, you can sign up for the rankings whenever you want, so come back another time.
Is that so? Well, registration's always open, so come back whenever you'd like to play a ranked match.
You're back again! How are your ranked matches going so far?
Hi there, champ. Defending your title okay?
What will it be today? Feel up to playing a Seiryo Cup match?
The bonus/penalty points for each rank are as follows.

1st  10,000 points
2nd  5,000 points
3rd  -5,000 points
4th  -10,000 points

1st  20,000 points
2nd 10,000 points
3rd -10,000 points
4th -20,000 points

1st  30,000 points
2nd 10,000 points
3rd -10,000 points
4th -30,000 points

1st  60,000 points
2nd 30,000 points
3rd -30,000 points
4th -60,000 points
Hey, buddy. You want to play with us? I hate to admit it, but we're pretty bad.
Uncle Kaz! Buy me a <Color:8>Bean Paste Bun<Color:Default>, please!
(Looks like Haruka wants a <Color:8>Bean Paste Bun<Color:Default>.)
But I wanted a <Color:8>Bean Paste Bun<Color:Default>...
Welcome!
Hm? Don't I know ya from somewhere?

Oh, got it! You're the guy who came in with Nakajima-san.
Thanks for comin' back. Your name was...
Suzuki.
Right, right, Suzuki-san! You know your boss is a regular here? When he gets tipsy, he always starts talkin' about ya.
Does he now?
Yep. "Our new hire, a fella named Suzuki-san. Looks serious as all get-out, always wears a frown cuttin' ditches in his forehead," he says.
I heard the story, but he wasn't kiddin'. You look like you could stare down a bull in mid-charge!
...I don't mean to scare you.
Haha, I'm just yankin' your chain. Tell ya what, though. Nakajima-san's taken a real shine to ya.
He's always singin' yer praises for workin' so hard all the time. Says he's mighty grateful to have ya on board.
...He really said that?
Yep. Oh, ya know what? Your order's on me today. Don't be shy about fillin' your belly, either.
No, I couldn't possibly⑬
It's fine! Nothin' to worry about. Nakajima-san's always done right by us, so it's the least I can do.
That's... very generous of you. Thank you.
So, what're ya havin'?
Ramen, please.
Aye! One ramen comin' up! How firm, buddy?
How... firm?

Yeah. Our noodles come in six levels of firmness:
Very soft, soft, regular, hard, very hard, and dunked.

Us Hakata locals, we like our noodles on the firm side.
"Dunked" is just dunkin' the noodles to remove the flour.
I'd recommend "very hard" for newbies.
Then I'll try very hard, please.
Aye! One ramen very hard, comin' right up!
Well? Tasty, wasn't it?
It was. I'm surprised at how much those extra firm noodles absorb the flavor of the broth. Gives it a very rich taste.
Well, ain't that a treat to hear! Welcome to the world of Hakata ramen. Next time bring that boss of yours, will ya?
Sure. But I really should be paying.
I said it's on me, Suzuki-san. Ya don't need to get so uptight about it.
Hey, no buts! Just enjoy.
You sure?
I'm sure, I'm sure.
Even so...
Suzuki-san! That's about enough⑬
Yeeeeooooowww!
(Is he okay?)
Oogh... Ouch! Damn...
Agh, it's my back! I went at it too hard with my old lady last night!
...Did you maybe throw out your back? If so, you need to get to a doctor.

No... Not now... There'll be a bum-rush of customers soon.
Like a waterfall of them. We call it "the Niagara of Death."
The... Niagara of Death?
Yep. That's when we pull the most business in. Can't afford to leave the place now.
Urk... But with this wretched spine of mine, I can barely stand, let alone boil noodles... Agh, what am I gonna do?
I know! How about you fill in behind the counter, just for now?
You want me to do it?
Yeah. The soup and the toppings are all ready to go. All's ya gotta do is boil the noodles and shlup 'em into bowls. Nothing complicated.
I doubt it's that simple...
It <Italic>is</Italic> that simple! Now come on, I'm beggin' ya! If I close up shop now, we'll be hurtin' for cash flow down the road.
Besides, I don't wanna disappoint the folks who come specifically lookin' for us.
(Well, he is a friend of the chief's... and I do owe him for the ramen. I should help the man.)
Okay. I'm not sure how well I can do, but I'll try to help you out.
Ya will!? Oh, you're a savior! No wonder Nakajima-san sees so much in ya. I'll pay ya for your time, too.
Hey, you got room for four?
Yep! Sit wherever ya like and I'll be right with ya!
Look at you, Suzuki-san! Lookin' good in an apron!

All right. Now, it's about to start! The time when customers
and orders come crashing down like a mighty waterfall of
chaos and confusion! It's time for the Niagara of Death!

...So, all I need to do is boil noodles to the firmness that
customers request?
Yup, that's all there is to it. Remember, it's all about firmness. Life is about firmness. Good luck!
(Okay, what to eat?)
(Let's check out the restaurant.)
